title: Novenas
hookLine: nine days of prayer, after the apostles waiting for the Spirit

cards: What would you keep doing for nine days straight, for someone else? A woman's brother is having surgery next week. Her aunt hands her a folded leaflet: a short prayer, the same each day, nine days of it.
Start tonight, the aunt says, and you'll finish before he goes in. She has never done anything like it and isn't sure what it will do. But nine days is something she can hold in her hands.

teach.b: A novena is nine days of prayer, for one intention or to prepare for a feast. The prayer can be short and the same each day, or a new reflection daily.
What makes it a novena is the shape: nine days, kept one after another. Tradition traces that shape to the apostles.
In Acts, before he ascends, Jesus tells them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father. So they wait, and pray, and the Spirit comes at Pentecost.
Tradition counts that waiting as nine days and calls it the first novena; that's tomorrow's story. There are many kinds. Some novenas prepare for a feast, like Christmas or a saint's day.
Some ask for something: work, healing, a safe birth. Some are for someone who has just died. Some ask a saint to pray alongside.
A novena isn't a vending machine: nine coins in, one answer out.
Some leaflets promise that a certain novena never fails. The Church doesn't teach that; the Catechism warns against treating any prayer as if its power came from saying it correctly.
Jesus says in Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims: "And when you are praying, speak not much, as the heathens. For they think that in their much speaking they may be heard." What does it do?

teach.h: WAIT FOR THE PROMISE OF THE FATHER.
teach.b: It brings a person back to the same intention day after day, long after the first rush of worry has faded. Day one is easy. Day six, when nothing seems to be happening, may be where the real praying starts.
Nine days is practice in waiting, the way the apostles waited, without knowing when or how the answer will come.

how: Catholics pray novenas, nine consecutive days of prayer, before feasts such as Christmas, for particular needs, for the dead, or asking a saint's intercession; parishes sometimes hold public novenas with a prayer service each evening.

games.q: a leaflet says its novena never fails, as long as you don't skip a word. what does Catholic teaching say?
o: it's true, if every word is said.
prayer's power doesn't come from saying it correctly.
it works only if you pass the leaflet on.
games.why: the Catechism warns against treating prayer as if its power lay in correct repetition, and Jesus says not to speak much, as if many words would be heard.

practice: Bring to mind one person or need weighing on you, and name it in a few words: that's your intention. If you pray, choose a prayer you know, the Our Father or the Hail Mary, and say it once a day for nine days, beginning now.
If you don't, keep the shape anyway: one minute a day, for nine days, holding that person in mind.
